articles.title: El problema que España debe solucionar durante este parón
articles.standfirst: Ganó el Mundial encajando un solo gol y ha recibido cinco en las primeras cuatro jornadas de la Nations League
articles.summary: Ganó el Mundial encajando un solo gol y ha recibido cinco en las primeras cuatro jornadas de la Nations League
articles.body: España atraviesa un momento inmejorable. La Selección no pierde un partido desde marzo de 2024, cuando cayó en un amistoso frente a Colombia, y acumula éxitos que han elevado las expectativas hasta un nivel difícil de imaginar. Sin embargo, cuando un equipo se acostumbra a ganar, también aumenta la exigencia. Y el combinado de Luis de la Fuente tiene un pequeño problema que corregir durante este parón de selecciones: su rendimiento defensivo. La clasificación para los cuartos de final de la Nations League ya está garantizada después del pleno de victorias (4/4) conseguido en la Fecha FIFA de septiembre-octubre. Pero hay un dato que invita a la reflexión. España llegó a esta competición después de conquistar el Mundial encajando un solo gol en todo el torneo y, sin embargo, ya ha recibido cinco tantos en las cuatro primeras jornadas de la Nations League. Una diferencia que pone el foco sobre una faceta del juego que había sido una de las grandes fortalezas del equipo. La convocatoria de Luis de la Fuente también ha dejado una imagen llamativa: el seleccionador ha citado a cuatro porteros para estos dos encuentros. A los habituales Unai Simón, David Raya y Joan García se ha unido Álvaro Valles, que está firmando un extraordinario comienzo de temporada con el Betis. Una competencia poco habitual bajo palos que refleja las alternativas con las que cuenta el técnico... aunque el verdadero reto pasa por recuperar la solidez colectiva que caracterizó a España en sus últimos grandes éxitos. Las apuestas deportivas también ponen el foco en la capacidad de la Selección para dejar su portería a cero. La primera oportunidad para corregir esta tendencia llegará a domicilio frente a una República Checa que no está destacando, precisamente, por su capacidad goleadora. El conjunto checo apenas ha marcado dos tantos en las cuatro jornadas disputadas, aunque uno de ellos llegó precisamente contra España en el encuentro celebrado en el Tartiere. Bet365 paga a 1.83 que los locales se queden sin marcar. Una cuota que refleja la confianza en la defensa española pese a los últimos registros encajados. En cualquier caso, esas pequeñas dudas defensivas no han reducido la confianza en España de cara a la conquista del título. Bet365 mantiene a la Selección como principal favorita para levantar la Nations League, con una cuota de 3.0. Por detrás aparecen Francia, con 3.75, e Inglaterra, con 5.5. Las mejores casas de apuestas siguen viendo al equipo de Luis de la Fuente un escalón por encima de sus principales rivales. El objetivo durante este parón será demostrar que, además de mantener su extraordinario potencial ofensivo, España también puede recuperar la fortaleza defensiva que le llevó a lo más alto.

articles.title: Iván Modia: "Dubái no va a dejar de invertir para convertirse en una capital mundial del pádel"
articles.standfirst: El director del P1 de Dubái explica en MARCA cómo es la gestión de un torneo de este calibre, el crecimiento del pádel en los Emiratos Árabes y la llegada de Courtois a su proyecto
articles.summary: El director del P1 de Dubái explica en MARCA cómo es la gestión de un torneo de este calibre, el crecimiento del pádel en los Emiratos Árabes y la llegada de Courtois a su proyecto
articles.body: Tras la celebración del Mundial, es tiempo de que vuelva la competición a Premier Padel y lo hace con uno de los torneos más destacados de la temporada: el P1 de Dubái. Pese a la ausencia de las dos primeras parejas del masculino y a que la pelea por el número uno está cerrada en el masculino y prácticamente sentenciada en el femenino, las principales figuras vuelven a copar todas las miradas en la ciudad emiratí. Sin embargo, detrás de todo el espectáculo hay figuras que hacen posible el correcto funcionamiento de eventos de esta magnitud y en este caso uno de los nombres propios es Iván Modia, CEO de Gallop Global y director del Emaar Dubái P1 de Premier Padel, que cuenta a MARCA cómo es la organización de esta cita y cómo se está viviendo la expansión del pádel en los Emiratos Árabes. Pregunta: Semana intensa, Iván. ¿Cómo está, cómo afronta estos días? Respuesta: La verdad es que muy bien. Es nuestro tercer año aquí en Dubái y creo que el inicio del torneo fue el más espectacular que se haya visto nunca. La pista que montamos a los pies del Burj Khalifa, teniendo a los mejores jugadores del mundo —al final Galán no pudo estar por lesión, pero estuvo Juan justo el día después de ganar el Mundial—, con las cuatro mejores jugadoras y los cuatro mejores jugadores del torneo, y con personalidades como Iniesta, Paula Badosa, Sheikh Zayed o Sania Mirza, personas con mucho poder aquí... Creo que el inicio ha sido espectacular. Las preparaciones han sido intensas, pero ver el resultado siempre es muy satisfactorio. P: ¿No les perjudica un poco que el torneo venga justo después del Mundial? Por la intensidad de la semana en Doha y por la acumulación de partidos, ¿no cree que les hubiera beneficiado tener una semana de descanso? R: No, la verdad es que creo que los jugadores vienen con las ganas de finalizar el tour de Oriente Próximo de la mejor manera posible. Como le digo, estar a final de temporada a nosotros nos viene bastante bien; creo que es un poquito al revés. Sí que es verdad que en un mundo ideal a lo mejor una semana de descanso hubiese estado bien, pero creo que, ya que están aquí, los jugadores tienen que continuar sin descanso para que luego puedan volver a casa y descansar de verdad. Irse y luego volver hubiese sido más perjudicial para ellos. Y a nosotros como torneo se nos refleja en la venta de entradas: no es que haya decaído el interés, sino que estamos bastante por encima de los números del año pasado. El interés sigue siendo muy alto a pesar de los pesares. P: ¿Cómo es organizar un torneo de este calibre? R: Son muchos meses de preparación y mucha ayuda de nuestros partners y del gobierno. Requiere mucha preparación y un buen equipo. Nosotros lo que estamos intentando es ser el mejor torneo del mundo. Sé que a lo mejor suena un poco pretencioso, pero realmente es el objetivo a medio plazo. Poco a poco, cada año vamos mejorando cosas. Este año hemos hecho mucho énfasis en reforzar la experiencia del jugador, para que se sienta más en casa que nunca: les hemos puesto en un hotel nuevo, un sistema de transporte nuevo y un Players' Lounge con todas las facilidades, incluyendo una de sus opciones favoritas, que es açaí para todos. Escuchamos mucho al jugador para que se sienta bien. Creo que la experiencia del jugador es lo primero que reforzamos, pero también la del aficionado. Hay mucha más inversión este año que en los anteriores y creo que se nota y se va a notar. P: ¿Cuáles son las mayores dificultades que se han encontrado en años anteriores y de cara a este? R: El primer año fuimos outdoor, hicimos el torneo donde se celebra el ATP 500 de tenis. Por supuesto es un sitio icónico, pero tanto para el espectador como para el jugador supuso una semana con un poquito más de calor de la cuenta y mucha humedad. Ese fue el primer reto que tuvimos que afrontar. Por eso, el año pasado lo trajimos indoor, al Hamdan Sports Complex. Más que una dificultad, un reto satisfactorio fue cómo podíamos transformar dos piscinas olímpicas —una de saltos y una normal—, vaciarlas y montar cuatro pistas de competición encima. Es un proceso que lleva como tres semanas, solo sacar el agua de las piscinas tarda cuatro días. Nivelarlo todo para poner las pistas encima con el peso que eso tiene y sin elevarlo a donde está la grada fue el reto más grande, porque nunca se había hecho antes. Pero eso lo hace especial también, y cuando haces un trabajo tan largo y tan intenso, ver el resultado te satisface más. P: En cuanto a objetivos, ¿cuáles son los principales que se marcan? R: El principal objetivo es hacer un evento digno de lo que está haciendo Dubái. Dubái lleva desde 2013 intentando desarrollar el deporte a todos los niveles, no únicamente desde la federación o el gobierno, sino que también se ha convertido en un sitio donde a los jugadores les gusta venir a vivir. Obviamente este año ha sido un poco particular por las circunstancias geopolíticas en la región y ha habido alguno que vino y luego se fue, pero el reto principal es que se convierta en un hub del pádel. Con la intención de Premier Padel de que el tour sea más internacional que nunca y que se vaya a nuevos sitios en el mundo, Dubái tiene una ubicación muy buena: estamos a mitad de camino entre Asia y Europa. Si el jugador tuviera que irse a Australia o a Asia y viviera en Dubái, estaría mejor. La ubicación y, sobre todo, el apoyo gubernamental que tiene el deporte lo hace un sitio muy atractivo. Nosotros nos tenemos que consolidar como un hub del pádel a nivel mundial, más allá de lo que es el torneo en sí. P: ¿Cómo es la gestión de los jugadores, que poco a poco se están convirtiendo casi en estrellas? ¿Cómo es gestionar a tantas grandes figuras? R: La verdad es que es un trato muy entrañable el que tenemos con ellos. Yo vengo del tenis, antes era director de evento en las finales de la Copa Davis, y es una experiencia un poco diferente, pero no tanto. Los jugadores de pádel son personas muy cercanas, gente a la que ves cada día y te intentan ayudar a mejorar. Están a una llamada de distancia, ellos o sus managers, siempre intentando sumar y sin poner dificultades. El feedback que nos dan es el que utilizamos para hacer el torneo mejor. Me parece que los jugadores están creciendo al mismo tiempo que el deporte y es muy fácil llevarlo con ellos. P: Usted que viene del tenis, siempre existe esa eterna comparación. ¿Qué diferencias nota entre la gestión de torneos de tenis y lo que es actualmente el pádel? R: Creo que el pádel está intentando marcar su propio camino y está aprendiendo. Nosotros como promotores, el tour o los jugadores estamos aprendiendo poco a poco, año a año. En el tenis todos los procesos están ya muy establecidos. Cuando sale alguna noticia en el pádel de un cambio aquí o allá, creo que es lógico porque el tenis lleva construyendo el deporte muchos más años. Pero a nivel de funcionamiento, de cómo operan Premier Padel, la Federación Internacional o la federación local, ya tienen muchos procesos del tenis. Lo que sí es verdad es que el pádel como negocio tiene que dar todavía muchos pasos para llegar hasta ahí, y eso es totalmente natural por la longevidad de un deporte y del otro. P: En ese sentido, por ejemplo en Doha la afluencia ha ido a más año a año. ¿Cómo hacen para intentar llevar un deporte tan nuevo a la gente de Dubái y lograr que cada año se vendan más entradas? R: Recibimos bastante gente de toda la región, así que hemos ido ampliando la pista central año a año. El primer año teníamos capacidad para unos 5.500 espectadores, el año pasado para 7.500 y este año estaremos sobre los 8.300 para la final. Hemos ido ampliando simplemente porque el mercado nos lo sigue pidiendo; si sigue así, el año que viene la tendré que volver a ampliar. ¿Cómo los traes al evento? Dándoles la mejor experiencia posible. Nosotros tratamos el Dubái P1 como si fuera un torneo de tenis indoor de los buenos históricos. Queremos ese nivel de que se vea por la tele que estás en un torneo premium. Cuando les proporcionas eso, la gente vuelve. Aquí funciona mucho el boca a boca, que es lo más importante. Emiratos tiene 11 millones de habitantes y Dubái casi 5. Para llegar a una audiencia que es más limitada, estamos llegando a casi todos, lo cual es muy complicado. Y que siga creciendo demuestra que también viene gente de fuera. El énfasis en el marketing digital para empujar la venta de entradas más allá de la ciudad de Dubái es la clave para seguir creciendo. P: ¿Pero la gente por la calle conoce el pádel o todavía está en ese proceso? R: Es fanática del pádel. Desde el COVID el deporte explotó aquí. Si quieres ir a un club a jugar al pádel después de trabajar, a las 6 o 7 de la tarde, es imposible encontrar pistas si no las reservas una semana o 10 días antes. Hay gente que se reserva una pista en el mejor club a las 7 de la tarde durante todo el año simplemente por asegurarse tenerla. P: ¿Puede ser Dubái una de las futuras capitales del pádel a nivel mundial? R: Sí, totalmente. De hecho, cuando hicimos el análisis de cómo y dónde queríamos empezar —mis socios son emiratíes y yo venía de hacer la Davis—, nos preguntamos cuál podía ser la Davis aquí, y el pádel era la respuesta lógica. El fervor que hay y el apoyo gubernamental y de la federación van a hacer que no dejen de invertir para que se convierta en una capital mundial. Y este año hay un dato definitorio: nuestro nuevo title sponsor es EMAAR, que son los dueños del Burj Khalifa o del Dubai Mall, entre otras cosas. Es una de las marcas más reconocidas de Dubái a nivel mundial y puntera en el real estate. Ellos no se involucran tanto en sponsorizar eventos deportivos, así que el hecho de que tengan el deseo de entrar en el pádel y lo vean como una propiedad atractiva lo dice todo. Ayer anunciamos también como empresa, en Galop, la incorporación de Thibaut Courtois como accionista. Una de las primeras cosas que nos dijeron Gonzalo y Thibaut fue que era increíble que hubiéramos llegado a un acuerdo con EMAAR. Da mucho orgullo y demuestra lo que es el pádel aquí. P: Le iba a preguntar también por eso, por lo de Courtois. ¿Cómo surge su entrada en el proyecto y cuál ha sido su acogida? R: Ha sido un proceso de meses que empezó con Gonzalo (Vila), el socio de Thibaut, hace unos meses. Ellos siempre han tenido la intención de entrar en el pádel con Nextplay. Nosotros les presentamos nuestro proyecto porque queremos crecer como empresa más allá del Dubái P1. Nos reunimos en Madrid con Gonzalo y con Thibaut y mantuvimos muchas conversaciones a lo largo del año. Lo que ellos ven en Nextplay se alinea mucho con lo que queremos nosotros: no únicamente una estrategia para establecer el torneo entre los centrales del mundo, sino seguir creciendo en el pádel y en otros deportes hacia el mercado asiático y otras partes del mundo. Somos una empresa de Dubái que quiere ir de aquí hacia el mundo, y con alguien de la talla de Thibaut y el empuje empresarial de Gonzalo podemos lograr lo que queremos juntos. P: Se sabe que Courtois es un gran aficionado. ¿Hizo eso que tuviera algo que ver? R: Sí, por supuesto. Si no tuviera este gusto por el pádel no creo que hubiese dado este paso. Que Thibaut y Gonzalo hayan pensado en nosotros es porque estamos estableciendo una plataforma en el pádel y en la generación de eventos o propiedades nuevas desde cero. Que Thibaut sea un fanático del pádel y crea en su crecimiento ha sido un factor diferencial. P: A nivel de los jugadores que se han ido a vivir a Dubái, como Jon Sanz, Javi Garrido o Lucas Bergamini, ¿cree que puede ser una tendencia que siga creciendo? R: Los jugadores que vienen a vivir aquí buscan un buen lugar con buenas instalaciones donde les den todas las facilidades, y aquí tienen eso. Sé que están muy felices y que la vida en Dubái es muy fácil. Que estén jugadores profesionales de esa talla ayuda seguro al crecimiento del pádel a nivel local; esa es la intención. Si estableces buenas infraestructuras y una política de país detrás del deporte, atraes a este tipo de figuras, a entrenadores españoles y argentinos de muy buen nivel y a gente que viene a abrir academias. El anuncio reciente de Tapia y Coello teniendo su propio equipo en Abu Dabi con bandera de Emiratos en la Hexagon Cup es un indicativo de lo que va a seguir pasando. Estamos al inicio de una historia muy larga.

articles.title: Tom Brady's NFL Power Rankings: Was Bills' Win Convincing Enough To Move To No. 1?
articles.summary: The Bears won in Week 9, but it didn't look pretty. Was that enough for the Bills or 49ers to take the top spot in Tom Brady's power rankings.
articles.body: Typically, Tom Brady doesn't change the No. 1 spot in his power rankings if the team won the week before. However, the results from Week 9 might cause the GOAT to crown a new No. 1 team. The Chicago Bears didn't have the best showing after earning the No. 1 spot in Brady's power rankings last week, needing a buzzer-beating field goal to take down the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers, meanwhile, each picked up decisive wins, staking their claims to be the best team in the NFL. So, does Brady think we now have a new No. 1 team in the league? Here's Brady's latest power rankings. 10. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 9 ↓ Week 9 result: 35-12 win vs. New York Jets Brady's thoughts: Last week, I said to clean up the flags and the offense would be right back in it. And Kansas City was listening because they barely had a penalty all afternoon, and the Jets spent the whole day settling for field goals. After a slow start, the Chiefs scored the last 21 points, and K9 (Kenneth Walker) was dominating again. The pass rush got after it, and Travis Kelce even ran one in for fun. Patrick Mahomes breathing down everyone's neck from the 10 spot should scare everyone on this list. Atlanta's up next as the Chiefs try to look ahead to Thanksgiving in Buffalo. Up next: at Atlanta Falcons (Sunday) 9. Cincinnati BengalsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: Unranked ↑ Week 9 result: 34-17 win vs. Atlanta Falcons (in Spain) Brady's thoughts: Joe Burrow and the Bengals finally make their debut, and I may have been sleeping on this team. That's four straight wins, and they scored 30-plus in every single one of those. Joe Burrow threw three tuddies against Atlanta, ran in another and the Bengals didn't turn it over once. You know, Cincy doesn't have a great win on their résumé yet, but that could change against Pittsburgh on Sunday night with first place in the AFC North up for grabs. Burrow just keeps getting better and better every single week. He's got so much chemistry with his star wideouts. I love the way he's playing. He's got command. He's got all the physical tools. He's really coming into his own this year. Up next: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (Sunday) 8. Pittsburgh SteelersRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 10 ↑ Week 9 result: Bye Brady's thoughts: Speaking of the Steelers, they had the week off and watched Cincy pull even with them in the AFC North. Pittsburgh hasn't lost since that last Thursday night game in Cleveland, and they own the tiebreaker over Cincy after beating them back in September. Sunday night, somebody walks out of Ohio alone in first place. Get your popcorn ready. There's a reason why they call the AFC North the black and blue division. Hard-hitting teams, always good defenses and always in cold conditions. I love this division. I love that they always come to show out. And every team in this division is always tough to beat. Up next: at Cincinnati Bengals (Sunday) 7. Green Bay PackersRecord: 6-3Previous ranking: Unranked ↑ Week 9 result: 45-27 win at New England Patriots Brady's thoughts: Green Bay jumps up from outside the top 10 and all the way up to No. 7 after a dominant showing in Foxborough that shocked everyone, including me. The Pack dropped 45 on the Patriots. Jordan Love threw bombs all over the field, and that defense came up big with three INTs. And that knocks New England out of the top 10 and puts Green Bay in. Now Minnesota comes to Lambeau in a battle between two teams heading in opposite directions. Up next: vs. Minnesota Vikings (Sunday) 6. Detroit LionsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 6 Week 9 result: 19-9 win at Miami Dolphins Brady's thoughts: Detroit hasn't even lost since September, and this time the defense led the way as Miami never even found the end zone. Jake Bates didn't miss. Jahmyr Gibbs punched in the only touchdown for the Lions. They just keep stacking wins.Next up, a quick trip to Germany — as quick as that can be — against the Pats. And a local tip from me: avoid the beer hall, guys. Stick to carb loading with those pretzels. Up next: vs. New England Patriots (Sunday, in Germany) 5. Jacksonville JaguarsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 5 Week 9 result: 33-10 win at Baltimore Ravens Brady's thoughts: Jacksonville went into Baltimore on a short week and did what great teams do against rookie QBs: dominate. The defense held the Ravens under 60 passing yards. Cam Little went 4-for-4 on field goals. Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington hooked up for another long tuddy. That's a three-game lead in the division with Tennessee next, and Jacksonville might have this division wrapped up by Thanksgiving at this rate. Up next: at Tennessee Titans (Sunday) 4. Denver BroncosRecord: 7-2Previous ranking: 4 Week 9 result: 26-21 win at Carolina Panthers Brady's thoughts: Stop me if you've heard this before: Denver found a way to win in the fourth quarter again. They trailed Carolina late. They scored two touchdowns in the final quarter to take control and Bo Nix threw for two scores. And the Panthers helped out with about 10,000 yards in penalties. Five straight wins, first place in the AFC West and a bye week to rest up. Not bad for a team that never makes it easy on themselves. Up next: Bye 3. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 7-1Previous ranking: 3 Week 9 result: 38-17 win vs. Las Vegas Raiders Brady's thoughts: The Niners looked like a very well-rested team coming off a bye against Vegas on Sunday. San Francisco forced five turnovers, scored on one of them, and never punted the ball back. Brock Purdy had a hand in three touchdowns and the running game went for almost 200 yards. They're 7-1 and in command of the NFC West. It's rare to have any breathing room in that division. There are some really good football teams in that division. I know the Rams have not played as well as they've wanted, and the Seahawks as well. But the Niners always find a way to figure it out. They've been banged up with a lot of injuries, but they just keep churning out their wins. Up next: at Dallas Cowboys (Sunday) 2. Buffalo BillsRecord: 7-1Previous ranking: 2 Week 9 result: 23-6 win at Minnesota Vikings Brady's thoughts: Monday night in Minnesota was a statement. Forty-two minutes of time of possession from Josh Allen and the Bills on their way to a dominant win against the Vikings. That's seven straight games with a touchdown from James Cook, and 20-plus touchdowns for Josh this season. The Bills lead the league in scoring, and they've got the best record in the AFC. The No. 1 spot is in their sights. Up next: at New York Jets (Sunday) 1. Chicago BearsRecord: 7-2Previous ranking: 1 Week 9 result: 27-24 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Brady's thoughts: In my rankings, you've got to lose to fall out of the top spot. Caleb Williams definitely made it hard on himself with the four picks, but Chicago stays at No. 1 for now. Great teams have to win ugly sometimes. The defense created pressure all night. Cairo Santos came up clutch to win it in the final seconds. The Bears haven't lost since Caleb came back, and now they get a bye to clean things up. I'm going to have to think about this one, actually. What happens to the No. 1 team on a bye week? Maybe the door is open for Buffalo to force their way to the top. Tune in next week to find out. articles.title: Niraj Kumar wins 50m rifle 3P bronze, Olympics quota
articles.summary: Niraj Kumar gave himself and India a reason to celebrate as the rifle shooter won bronze and a quota place for the Los Angeles Games at the ISSF World
articles.body: Niraj Kumar gave himself and India a reason to celebrate as the rifle shooter won bronze and a quota place for the Los Angeles Games at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Wednesday. The Navy shooter won a hard-fought bronze after scoring 346.5 in the 8-men final of the men's 50m rifle 3position event, while independent athlete (Russian) Dmitrii Pimenov won gold and a quota place with the score of 362.8, a junior world record. Slovakia's Patrik Jany 357.2 won silver and a quota place.Another Indian, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, too had made it to the final, but finished fifth after scoring 323.7. Niraj, who hails from Punjab, top scored in qualification with 591, while Aishwary was fourth with 586.In the final, Niraj started off well and maintained second position almost throughout the final. However, a 9.4 in the 34th shot to slip to third position, as Patrik hit a 10.4 to surge ahead."It was a good match. I am happy to have won a medal and a quota place for the country. It was a tough medal to win as the weather was erratic and there was a lot of wind throughout the qualification round. It was not just about winning, it was putting all your experience together to deal with the wind," Niraj, 26, said. articles.title: ‘That’s enough’ – Skip Bayless slams JJ Redick for not trying to ‘save’ Luka Doncic from himself
articles.summary: Luka Doncic suffered an injury scare against the Milwaukee Bucks, and Skip Bayless believes JJ Redick is to blame. Luka Doncic seemed to injure his ankle due...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic suffered an injury scare against the Milwaukee Bucks, and Skip Bayless believes JJ Redick is to blame.

Luka Doncic seemed to injure his ankle due to a dangerous closeout from Kyle Kuzma in the fourth quarter of a blowout win for the Los Angeles Lakers.

Both players would end up leaving the game after getting hurt, but the Los Angeles Lakers still managed to earn a big win to extend their record to 11-2.

Skip Bayless questions JJ Redick not managing Luka Doncic's minutes amid injury scare

Taking to X following the Los Angeles Lakers' win against the Milwaukee Bucks, Skip Bayless criticised JJ Redick for not taking Luka Doncic out of the game before he injured his ankle.

He suggested that the Lakers were well on their way to a victory, and Redick should have ignored Doncic's desire to score 30 points in order to avoid the injury scare.

Bayless wrote: "No idea why Luka was still in this blowout – just turned his ankle with AR already gone due to heel injury. I realise Luka wanted to at least get his 30 – he wound up with 32 – but JJ has to save Luka from himself and say that's enough."

Bayless does make a valid point here. The Lakers had a significant lead at that point, and the Bucks were not making any efforts to mount a comeback.

While Doncic wanting to stay in the game and score 30 points is understandable, given that he had a rare poor shooting night and wanted to keep his streak of scoring 30+ points a game going, it was a risk that didn't need to be taken.

Last season, Doncic missed a significant portion of the regular season and the Lakers' entire playoff run due to an injury he sustained against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

There has been concern about Doncic's fitness and health since he joined the Lakers. Even though he has looked much healthier coming into this season, injuries can occur at any time, and the Lakers didn't need to take such an unnecessary risk with Doncic just to satisfy his desire to keep his individual numbers strong.

Thankfully, the injury doesn't appear to be serious, although more will be revealed tomorrow when the Lakers can conduct tests on Doncic's ankle.

articles.title: Bentley se asocia con el PSG, pero ni Fabián Ruiz ni Ferrán Torres tendrán coche gratis
articles.standfirst: El acuerdo durará hasta 2028 y pretende explorar de forma conjunta "el lujo, el diseño, la cultura y el deporte". Pero no todos son buenas noticias para los jugadores
articles.summary: El acuerdo durará hasta 2028
articles.body: Estamos acostumbrados a ver acuerdos comerciales entre marcas de coches y clubes de fútbol. BMW, por ejemplo, es en la actualidad socio del Real Madrid y entrega un coche a cada miembro del primer equipo, que les renueva cada año (pronto recibirán los nuevos). Hyundai hace lo mismo con el Atlético de Madrid y sus jugadores, y Cupra cumple la misma función en el F.C. Barcelona. Con estos antecedentes, confirmados por acuerdos similares entre marcas y la mayoría de los grandes clubes de Europa, entendemos que a los jugadores del Paris Saint-Germain les debió nacer un brillo en los ojos al enterarse de que la lujosa Bentley había llegado a un acuerdo con su club. Pero esta nueva asociación viene con una naturaleza diferente. Su objetivo es bastante más etéreo e indefinido. De hecho, y según la marca británica, lo que se pretende es que la marca y el club exploren "nuevas oportunidades para involucrar a sus comunidades a través de experiencias exclusivas, momentos cuidadosamente seleccionados y narrativas originales inspiradas en los mundos del lujo, el diseño, la cultura y el deporte". Cómo se plasmarán palabras tan bonitas en algo real es algo que no ha sido desvelado. Es decir, que los Hakimi, Vitinha, Fabián Ruiz, Dembélé y Ferrán Torres, además del propio Luis Enrique y el resto de la plantilla, se van a quedar sin el privilegio que supone configurar a su gusto el coche elegido (o asignado) y disfrutarlo durante un año entero, hasta que al siguiente se lo cambien por otro también personalizado a su estilo. Claro que muchos podrán decir, y con razón, que con el sueldo que cobran bien se lo pueden pagar sin provocar una debacle en sus cuentas corrientes. Este acuerdo se va a prolongar hasta 2028 y, para Christophe Georges, miembro del consejo de administración de Bentley, el París Saint-Germain "es un símbolo de la energía y la confianza del París moderno [...] A través de esta colaboración, esperamos unir a nuestras comunidades de formas nuevas y atractivas, al tiempo que celebramos la creatividad, la individualidad y la atención al detalle que definen a ambas marcas". Richard Heaselgrave, director de ingresos del París Saint-Germain, ha añadido que "esta colaboración refleja la capacidad del club para atraer a marcas icónicas, unidas por valores y ambiciones compartidos. Bentley representa una visión del lujo arraigada en un legado extraordinario, que resuena con nuestra propia identidad y nuestra incansable búsqueda de la excelencia".

articles.title: 5 Trade Landing Spots for Erik Karlsson Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: Changes could be coming soon for the Pittsburgh Penguins.
articles.body:
Changes could be coming soon for the Pittsburgh Penguins.

Six weeks into the regular season, they are floundering near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings. Most of their stars are aging, while many of their promising young players are still learning the ropes.

On Nov. 6, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas could become a seller in the trade market. He believed some moves could happen "pretty quickly," depending on the no-trade protection of some of the players and what type of return he can get for them.

Erik Karlsson could be among the players that Dubas is willing to move. He's in the final season of an eight-year contract , with the Penguins carrying $10 million of his $11.5 million cap hit. Karlsson also has a full no-movement clause, but he might accept a trade to a contender this season as a rental player.

Karlsson has frequently appeared on our NHL trade boards . A skilled puck-moving defenseman, he's the only active three-time winner of the James Norris Memorial Trophy. As of Nov. 10, the 36-year-old led the Penguins with 18 points in as many games.

Despite his age, cap hit, and no-movement clause, Karlsson could draw interest from teams with Stanley Cup aspirations looking for a mobile right-shot defenseman with offensive skills. Here are five potential landing spots.

The defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes are off to a great start, sitting in first place in the overall standings as of Nov. 10. Nevertheless, general manager Eric Tulsky has shown he's unafraid to make bold moves and could do so again to help his club win the Cup for the second straight season.

Perhaps Tulsky would consider pursuing Erik Karlsson. He'd likely do so closer to the March 1 trade deadline, when the Hurricanes will have accrued $31.7 million in salary cap space . That would make it easier to absorb the remainder of his cap hit.

Karlsson was linked to the Hurricanes during the summer of 2025 . While things have changed for the club since then, his skills as a big-minute, puck-moving, right-shot defenseman could provide a boost of experienced skill on the right side of their blue line .

The Hurricanes could offer up 26-year-old center Jesperi Kotkaniemi as part of the return. Alexander Nikishin could interest the Penguins if the 25-year-old defenseman is willing to sign a contract extension. They also carry two third-round picks in 2027 and an extra first-rounder in 2028 to use as trade bait.

Erik Karlsson began his career with the Ottawa Senators in 2009-10. He spent many of his best seasons in Canada's capital, winning two of his three Norris Trophies there and helping the Senators come within one goal of reaching the 2017 Stanley Cup Final.

The Senators have spent years trying to find an experienced big-minute defenseman to fill the right side of their top defensive pairing . Karlsson has fond memories of his time with the Senators. According to Bruce Garrioch of the Ottawa Citize n, the club's fans would love to have him back .

It could take until close to the March 1 trade deadline, when the Senators will have accrued $11.5 million in cap space . Even then, they might prefer that the Penguins retain some salary, or the Senators might have to move a player in the deal.

The Senators might part with one of their two second-round picks in 2027 as part of the deal. However, the Penguins could prefer agitating forward Ridly Greig or promising defenseman Carter Yakemchuk.

Nikita Kucherov's decision not to re-sign with the Tampa Bay Lightning could force management to make one final push to win the Stanley Cup before the superstar winger departs via free agency next July.

Lightning general manager Julien BriseBois could consider adding an experienced top-pairing defenseman to the right side of his blue line. With over $16.4 million in accrued cap space by the March 1 trade deadline, he has room to take on the remainder of Erik Karlsson's contract.

BriseBois' predecessor, Steve Yzerman, nearly had a deal in place to acquire Karlsson from the Ottawa Senators during the summer of 2018 . However, the deal fell through, and he was eventually shipped to the San Jose Sharks.

Karlsson would be more affordable to acquire this time if the Lightning were interested. They could offer one of their two fourth-round picks in 2027 or one of their two third-round picks in 2028. However, the Penguins could prefer a young forward like Conor Geekie as part of the deal.

The Toronto Maple Leafs underwent significant roster changes this year under new general manager John Chayka. His biggest moves included acquiring winger Kirill Marchenko, signing defenseman Darren Raddysh and goalie Sergei Bobrovsky, and selecting Gavin McKenna with the first-overall pick in the 2026 NHL Draft.

Chayka might not be done tinkering with his roster, especially as the March 1 trade deadline approaches. He could scour the trade market in search of skilled depth for the right side of his blue line, especially given veteran defenseman Chris Tanev's injury history and Raddysh's struggles as their top-pairing rearguard.

Erik Karlsson could be on Chayka's radar. In August, speculation linked the Maple Leafs to the Penguins' defenseman, depending on where both teams were in the standings later in the season.

Acquiring Karlsson would likely require salary retention by the Penguins, an offsetting salary move by the Leafs, or a combination of the two.

Toronto could offer up its conditional 2027 first-rounder from the Avalanche if Karlsson were willing to sign an extension.

Erik Karlsson could be unwilling to waive his no-movement clause for a Western Conference team. However, if he's open to skating for a Western Conference contender as a playoff rental, the Utah Mammoth could be an interesting option.

On Nov. 4, Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic reported that Mammoth general manager Bill Armstrong was interested in goaltender Connor Hellebuyck before he was traded to New Jersey. He's also in on Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin and could monitor Nikita Kucherov's situation with the Lightning.

LeBrun also noted that Armstrong made significant roster additions over the past two years. He could try again near the trade deadline to bolster his roster for a deep playoff run. Depending on his blue line's performance, he might keep an eye on Erik Karlsson's status.

The Mammoth have over $15.8 million in projected accrued cap space at the March trade deadline. They also have plenty of draft picks and a deep pool of promising young talent to draw on as trade bait.

articles.title: The Roman Reigns Curse Crushing WWE
articles.summary: There is no denying that Roman Reigns has gotten better at professional wrestling.
articles.body:
There is no denying that Roman Reigns has gotten better at professional wrestling.

The Tribal Chief's character work has improved, his microphone skills are much stronger, and he's become a more compelling performer than the guy WWE spent years desperately trying to convince audiences was the next big thing.

Unfortunately, WWE seems to have mistaken improvement for greatness.

The Bloodline's Status Heading Into WWE Survivor Series WarGames🩸

Reigns is a very good wrestler, particularly in an era where the company's main-event depth leaves plenty to be desired. But the way WWE keeps positioning him suggests we're supposed to believe we're watching one of the greatest performers in wrestling history.

And the company's obsession with keeping Reigns at the center of everything is becoming a problem that extends far beyond one Superstar. The experiment worked once, but WWE's inability to move on from it is crushing the product.

WWE Keeps Chasing the Magic of Reigns' Bloodline Run

The original Bloodline storyline was one of WWE's best accomplishments in years. Reigns finally found a character that worked, surrounded himself with compelling personalities, and became the centerpiece of a story that consistently delivered.

But that was several years ago. The company has spent an absurd amount of time trying to recreate that magic, seemingly convinced that another lengthy championship reign or another Roman-led storyline will produce the same results.

The problem is that WWE continues treating The OTC like the answer to every question. Need a major storyline? Bring back Reigns. Need a championship to feel important? Put Reigns in the picture. Need a marquee main event? Somehow, Reigns ends up involved.

There is a difference between being a major star and being the only star WWE seems interested in protecting. Reigns has benefited from booking most wrestlers could only dream of, but the company has become so dependent on that formula that it no longer feels special.

Reigns Is Overrated, and WWE Is Making It Worse

I'll give Reigns credit where it's due. He's improved tremendously. His ability to control a match, work a crowd and deliver meaningful character moments is considerably better than it was a decade ago.

That doesn't make him an all-time great, though.

In fact, Reigns might be the most overrated wrestler in history when you consider the gap between how WWE presents him and what he actually brings to the table. He's good, sometimes very good, but the constant insistence that he's operating on a different level than everyone else has become exhausting.

His latest Crown Jewel victory over Sami Zayn is another example. Reigns already has world championships, an established legacy, and more accolades than he needs.

What exactly did winning the Men's Crown Jewel Championship accomplish? Did it elevate Zayn? Did it create a new star? Did it give WWE something it couldn't have accomplished without putting another trophy in Reigns' hands?

Of course not. It was another Reigns victory because apparently that's what WWE thinks its audience needs.

WWE's Reigns Obsession Is Holding Everyone Back

The biggest casualty of this obsession is the rest of the roster.

Talented performers should be getting opportunities to establish themselves as legitimate main event attractions. Instead, WWE continues operating as though everything eventually needs to revolve around Reigns.

Championship divisions suffer, emerging stars struggle to break through, and storylines take a back seat to maintaining The Tribal Chief's position. The irony is that WWE has spent years trying to convince audiences that Reigns is the undisputed face of the company, but that approach has arguably made the overall product less interesting.

Reigns doesn't need another championship. He doesn't need another lengthy run. And WWE certainly doesn't need to keep finding reasons to remind everyone how important he is.

The 41-year-old has earned his place as a major WWE Superstar, but he hasn't earned a lifetime exemption from criticism, nor should the company keep sacrificing its roster's development to preserve his position.

WWE needs to stop chasing The Bloodline's glory days and start creating new ones. Until that happens, Reigns might remain the company's biggest attraction, but he'll also continue being one of its biggest problems.

articles.title: England vs Croatia: UEFA Nations League – preview, team news, predictions
articles.summary: Harry Kane set to become England’s most capped player while Jude Bellingham could be joined by younger brother, Jobe.
articles.body:
Who: England vs Croatia What: UEFA Nations League, Group A3 Where: Wembley Stadium, London, United Kingdom When: Thursday, November 12 , at 8:45pm (19:45 GMT). How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:45 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Harry Kane will lead with a spring in his step and a newly acquired Ballon d’Or trophy on his arm as England host Croatia in a Nations League clash, with a spot in the quarterfinals up for grabs.

The England captain will be man of the hour on Thursday after a prolific few weeks that saw him win the coveted individual honour and he will present the trophy in front of home fans ahead of the match at Wembley Stadium.

Kane, 33, will also become England’s most-capped men’s player, making his 126th appearance. This surpasses the record set in 1990 by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who will be in attendance to mark the occasion.

The Bayern Munich forward is also England’s record scorer with 91 goals.

“Definitely up there with the biggest [achievements of my career],” England captain Kane told reporters at former club Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Wednesday after being given a standing ovation when he entered the room.

“It showcases consistency at the highest level and to reach the number of caps I have is a testament to the things I spoke about in my [Ballon d’Or] speech behind the scenes, the dedication, and for sure it is one of the biggest milestones of my career.”

Tuchel said Kane was the “perfect captain and a leader by example” and described his playing style as unique, adding that he is getting smarter with age.

Manager Tuchel also said he has no intention of leaving the England job before the 2028 European Championship regardless of any offers from major clubs.

England only need a draw to make it to the quarterfinals having won three and lost one of their four games so far. They sit second with nine points behind leaders Spain with 12 points, and both teams should make it to the last eight.

Croatia are seeking redemption after a 7-0 thrashing from England in their previous encounter last month, followed by a narrower 2-1 defeat to Spain.

The 2018 World Cup runners-up are third in the group, and manager Slaven Bilic emphasised the importance of finishing third to maintain their Nations League A status.

Czechia, meanwhile, have only won once and cannot reach the quarterfinals.

England will travel to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday while Croatia take on Czechia in a home fixture.

Bellingham brothers could feature together

A major talking point for England’s squad selection was the exclusion of midfielder Cole Palmer. But a more captivating storyline is that of Jobe Bellingham finally playing alongside older brother and England star Jude.

The younger Bellingham received his maiden senior call-up after impressing at Borussia Dortmund and England’s under-21 side, which he captains.

Jude had previously said it would be the highlight of his career, while Jobe said it would be an emotional milestone.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said.

If he features against Croatia, they will be the 22nd set of brothers to play for England and the first since Gary and Phil Neville in 2007.

What happened in the last England vs Croatia game?

England ran riot in Rijeka last month to obliterate Croatia 7-0 thanks to a brace each from Kane and Bukayo Saka, while Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers were also on target.

Tuchel’s men took just eight minutes to go ahead with an incisive raid that exposed the talent gap between the sides.

“It was the highest level from everyone and from first to last minute as well,” Tuchel said, summing up his side’s dominance.

Tuchel: “For us, it’s important not to chase the same result … we want to win the match to have a chance to win in Spain, and that’s where our focus is. We expect a reaction from Croatia and we expect to overcome this mental challenge for us to start from scratch.”

Bilic: “I told the players that the way we played against Spain last month is our standard. That is how we want to play, with togetherness, aggression and everything else. Tomorrow we have a chance to show that what happened in Rijeka was just a collective bad day.”

The Opta supercomputer heavily favours England, with a win probability of 67.2 percent.

Croatia were assigned a mere 14.8 percent chance, while a draw was estimated at an 18 percent likelihood.

October 3, 2026: Croatia 0-7 England (Nations League)

June 17, 2026: England 4-2 Croatia (FIFA World Cup)

June 13, 2021: England 1-0 Croatia (European Championship)

November 18, 2018: England 2-1 Croatia (Nations League)

October 12, 2018: Croatia 0-0 England (Nations League)

England will be without defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence — both expected to recover for Sunday’s clash against Spain — and Tuchel is looking at James Hill for cover.

Marc Guehi is out with a hip injury and has been replaced by Dan Burn. Jarrad Branthwaite, Jarell Quansah and Ben White could all be in contention at centre-back.

Saka, who scored twice in Rijeka, was not named in the squad because of a quadriceps injury that is set to keep him out for weeks.

Myles Lewis-Skelly is suspended after being booked in both games against Czechia, while Declan Rice, back after missing the last camp, should partner Elliot Anderson in midfield.

Predicted starting XI: Jordan Pickford (goalkeeper), Lewis Hall, James Hill, Dan Burn, Ben White, Declan Rice, Elliot Anderson, Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Harry Kane

Veteran winger Ivan Perisic will miss the match after receiving a red card against Spain.

Josip Sutalo, Marin Pongracic, Andrej Kramaric and Franjo Ivanovic are also unavailable, with Luka Vuskovic and Duje Caleta-Car expected to start against England’s attack.

Luka Sucic has a fever and is almost certain to miss the game, while Kristijan Jakic is reported to be out of both Nations League games with a knee ligament injury.

articles.title: The State of Roman Reigns' The Bloodline Heading Into WWE Survivor Series WarGames
articles.summary: Roman Reigns is having one of the best years of his career—if not his best—in 2026, delivering an extraordinary run of in-ring performances and a World Heavyweight Championship reign that may be his finest yet.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns is having one of the best years of his career—if not his best—in 2026, delivering an extraordinary run of in-ring performances and a World Heavyweight Championship reign that may be his finest yet.

Yes, that includes his nearly four-year run as undisputed WWE universal champion.

How has that success helped or hurt the reunited, revamped Bloodline as they prepare to face The 946 in WarGames at Survivor Series in Houston on November 28?

Reigns has always had a magnetism that draws his family back into the fold, regardless of the circumstances surrounding their latest falling-out.

In 2024, after the group's prolonged disintegration, Jimmy and Jey Uso stood by his side against Solo Sikoa's Bloodline, even though Jey had escaped the toxic relationship to become his own man and a singles star.

It made sense, then, that the twins would reunite with Reigns amid CM Punk's disrespect toward their family before and after WrestleMania 42.

Jacob Fatu was forced to join after losing to Reigns at a premium live event, while Solo Sikoa realigned himself with The OTC after being attacked and abducted by The 946. Both alliances are rooted in necessity rather than choice, but they at least make sense narratively.

The feud with The 946 has been beneficial for two reasons.

First, it has made the group stronger. Sikoa previously opposed his family and went to war with his own brothers to prevent their return to dominance in WWE. Now, he is ready to fight alongside them against Royce Keys and Co.

Fatu adds further strength to the group, though he has made it clear that he is there only to serve The Tribal Chief—not The Usos or anyone else in the faction.

Confronted with a shared enemy, he stands side by side with his family to get revenge for the hell they have been put through in recent months.

Second, The Bloodline is using its credibility and main-event status to elevate a new group in WWE.

Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Lucien Prince, Bronco Nima and Jaida Parker have suddenly become featured players on WWE television, benefiting directly from their association with Reigns and Co. and the group's star power.

Regardless of how it came about—or whether revisiting the group two years after its demise was necessary—the renewed Bloodline has been a success, if only for its role in elevating a brand-new heel faction. Those fresh antagonists have helped revitalize a WWE product that had grown stagnant before their arrival.

The OTC is still the egotistical champion that he was two or three years ago. Today, he understands the value of his family rather than taking them for granted, as he did during The Bloodline's original run from 2021-24.

The world champion and one of the most popular wrestlers on the planet, Reigns has delivered on the mic and in the ring this year, ensuring whatever he is part of is among the highlights of any show.

Jimmy has repeatedly returned to Reigns' side, even going to war against his own brother in 2024. It is no surprise that he willingly dropped everything to join his cousin's crusade to run WWE again.

Jey's return was more of a surprise, especially since he had become his own man and won the very world title Reigns carries today. Still, the seeds for a reunion were planted when The Tribal Chief criticized him for YEETing and having fun, losing the world title, and losing sight of the empire the family was trying to build.

The twins have built up credibility with fans and can headline shows when Reigns is unavailable without missing a beat. Plus, there is always the opportunity for Jey to step out of line and challenge Reigns again, given his past success.

Fatu arrived in WWE as part of Sikoa's Bloodline and later fought against Reigns and his allies.

So, it makes sense that The Samoan Werewolf would be reluctant to stand side by side with The OTC and his cousins and battle anyone in their path.

The 946's savage attacks, including Parker running Fatu over with an SUV, changed things. They brought the group together and eliminated any hesitation Fatu may have had about standing firmly with The Bloodline at Survivor Series.

The big man is as over as ever and in as strong a position as at any point in his WWE run, thanks to his relationship with The Bloodline.

If there is one Superstar who has been hurt by his sudden reunion with The Bloodline, it's Sikoa.

Over the summer, the second-generation star was able to show off his enormous personality and win over the audience. He was building momentum in a rivalry with The Usos and Fatu, and he looked like the next big breakout star from the storied Samoan wrestling dynasty.

Now, he is back in The Bloodline, another face in the crowd. He has a renewed serious side, sure, but the progress he made in developing a new side of his character—one that connected with audiences—has been sacrificed for the Survivor Series story with The 946.

Hopefully, Sikoa can break away after WarGames and regain some of that momentum. He is the only member of The Bloodline who would be better off on his own.

The immediate future is far more difficult to forecast than the long term.

By WrestleMania 43, The Bloodline should be busy serving as tackling dummies for Oba Femi.

With all signs pointing to a showdown between Reigns and The Ruler, The Usos, Fatu and Sikoa are likely to provide opposition for Femi in the buildup to the year's biggest match.

It would not be surprising to see Fatu emerge as a challenger for Femi's world title in the wake of WrestleMania—assuming WWE does the right thing and crowns The Ruler rather than making fans wait another year.

Until then, do not be surprised if The Bloodline continues its rivalry with The 946 through the holidays and into the Royal Rumble.

WWE likely did not spend time building The 946 into a legitimate threat to The Bloodline just to abandon the rivalry after WarGames, even if the match typically serves as a feud-ending showdown.

Tag matches and singles bouts leading up to the Royal Rumble on February 6 make sense, perhaps culminating in Reigns defending his world title against Keys. That would give the entire group something to do until WWE's WrestleMania plans become clear.

Regardless, The Bloodline is likely to remain intact and prominent on WWE television in both the short and long term as the company sticks with a proven formula that draws interest—and money.

articles.title: Vivaan Kapoor wins silver at ISSF World Championship, secures India’s 2028 LA Olympics quota
articles.summary: India's Vivaan Kapoor narrowly missed out on a historic world title but had plenty to celebrate after clinching silver in the men's trap event at the ISSF
articles.body: India's Vivaan Kapoor narrowly missed out on a historic world title but had plenty to celebrate after clinching silver in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships on Thursday. The 24-year-old also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics with his impressive performance.The Jaipur shooter was within touching distance of becoming only the second Indian to claim a world championship title in men's trap. However, his gold-medal hopes ended in a shoot-off against Kuwait's Abdulrahman Alfaihan after both shooters finished tied at 29 out of 30 in regulation.With the contest going down to a decisive shoot-off, Kapoor missed a clay bird, allowing Alfaihan to take the top spot and settle for silver himself.Despite falling just short of gold, Kapoor's achievement added another significant chapter to India's history in men's trap shooting. He became only the fourth Indian to win a medal in the discipline at the World Championships, joining an illustrious group comprising Karni Singh, Manavjit Singh Sandhu and Zorawar Singh Sandhu.Manavjit remains the only Indian to have won a men's trap world title, having achieved the feat at the 2006 World Championships in Zagreb, Croatia. Karni Singh had previously claimed silver, while Zorawar Singh Sandhu also figured among India's World Championship medallists in the event.Kapoor's silver medal also carried an important Olympic significance. He became the third Indian shooter to secure a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, following men's 10m air pistol shooter Jaypal Malviya and men's 50m rifle 3-positions bronze medallist Niraj Kumar.For Kapoor, the World Championships podium finish represents a major breakthrough, even as the missed opportunity in the shoot-off leaves him agonisingly close to a historic gold medal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Canada won’t let Russian players enter for ice hockey junior championship
articles.summary: Russian, Belarusian athletes and officials will be prevented from entering Canada regardless of their visa status.
articles.body:
Canada says it will prevent Russian athletes and officials from entering the country for ice hockey’s World Junior Championship in Alberta, effectively barring their participation weeks before the tournament begins.

Canada’s Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden said on Wednesday that Ottawa opposes Russian and Belarusian participation in international sport “as long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine with Belarus’s complicity”.

The minister for immigration, refugees and citizenship “will take measures to individually assess and prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering Canada to compete, regardless of whether they already hold valid visas”, Van Koeverden said.

Hockey Canada has previously said it supports the government’s position.

Late last month, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ordered the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) to admit Russian teams to five upcoming championships, beginning with the World Junior Championship.

The IIHF, which has barred Russia from most international competitions since Moscow’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, said it disagreed with the CAS decision.

The hockey federation’s statement followed announcements from Norway, Denmark, Sweden and the Czech Republic that ⁠⁠their national teams will refuse to play against Russia at next year’s men’s World Championships in Germany.

Latvia and Finland have also said their teams will not play Russia, while the Finnish city of Turku threatened to ⁠⁠drop its hosting duties for the 2028 World Junior Championship.

Belarus’s team will not participate in the championship following a separate decision by the IIHF.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has previously said Ottawa would not permit Russian athletes to compete for their country on Canadian soil, a statement some perceived as keeping the door open for their participation as neutrals.

Van Koeverden said Canada allowed neutral participation only by individual athletes, ruling out the option for the Russian team.

“Canada’s position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual,” he said. “Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.”

The World Junior Championship runs from December 26 to January 5.

articles.title: New WWE Rumors on Bronson Reed's Injury Following Report of Punctured Lung at Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: New details have emerged regarding the injuries that have resulted in WWE Superstar Bronson Reed being unable to travel back to the United States from Saudi Arabia following last weekend's Crown Jewel premium live event.
articles.body:
New details have emerged regarding the injuries that have resulted in WWE Superstar Bronson Reed being unable to travel back to the United States from Saudi Arabia following last weekend's Crown Jewel premium live event.

According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Reed broke multiple ribs and suffered a lacerated kidney.

It had previously been reported by Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter that Reed was dealing with broken ribs and a punctured lung as a result of the spot that saw Oba Femi toss him off the stage and through some tables.

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp was the first to report that Reed had not returned to the U.S. with the rest of the WWE roster and staff because of injury.

Sapp noted that Reed stayed back with a "top international executive and a member of [WWE's] medical team."

While Reed did not wrestle at Crown Jewel, he played a significant role in the result of the World Tag Team Championship match.

The 38-year-old Aussie attempted to interfere on behalf of The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory during their title defense against Penta and Je'Von Evans.

However, Femi showed up to even the odds, which is when he threw Reed off the stage.

No additional information has been released regarding when Reed may be able to fly home or how long he will have to be out of action.

Until then, The Vision will continue to be shorthanded, as Logan Paul remains on the shelf as well due to a torn triceps.

articles.title: Steve Borthwick explains Max Ojomoh selection against Japan: ‘One of the most talented players in English rugby’
articles.summary: Ojomoh will wear the No 12 shirt after an injury to Seb Atkinson
articles.body:
The England head coach Steve Borthwick has described Max Ojomoh as "one of the most talented players in English rugby" after recalling the centre to his starting side to face Japan.

Ojomoh is in line for his first international appearance in nearly a year after earning selection in a much-changed backline, wearing No 12 following an injury to Seb Atkinson.

The Bath midfielder won player of the match in his last England outing against Argentina in November of last year, but then fell out of favour, spending periods out of Borthwick's squad.

But with Atkinson absent and Benhard Janse van Rensburg stood down from this campaign as he works his way back from concussion, Ojomoh has got the nod ahead of Fraser Dingwall as Henry Slade 's centre partner.

Borthwick has challenged Ojomoh to put his best game on the park at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium in the Nations Championship clash – so long as he and the rest of England's individuals stick to the team's strategy.

"Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby. I think that's undeniable. You can see what he can do with the ball in his hands," said Borthwick. "That's one of the reasons why I'm looking forward to seeing him out there on Saturday.

"The team is always the most important thing, at the same time, it's the balance between the team, self-sacrifice, and self-expression. You've got players there that when the moment is right, and they'll judge the moment, that self-expression comes through. So [wing] Will Joseph can get his hands on the ball and back himself in those moments. Go and beat the man in front of him.

"Similarly for Max Ojomoh, there are always moments where players go and express themselves. Those moments will come more often when we're playing a really cohesive team performance. That's one of the challenges because this backline hasn't played together an awful lot.

"That's where George Ford , [ Jack van Poortvliet ], Freddie Steward , Henry Slade, those guys have got a huge role to play. I've said a lot about how I value experience, how I value those players who have been in the Test match arena a lot, those players have got a responsibility to help bring those younger players through."

Ojomoh is believed to have been asked to improve his work off-the-ball and cover more ground in both attack and defence, key ares of emphasis for England's centres.

Borthwick is hopeful that Atkinson, who had worn No 12 in six consecutive Tests, will be back fit to face New Zealand in a week's time.

The England head coach believes the role of a centre has become tougher and tougher as Test rugby has evolved.

"If you just track the centres and how quickly they move in attack from one side of the pitch to the other, [they have to have] the awareness to be alive," he explained. "If both centres are stuck on one side of the pitch defensively, one of them is probably going to have to get to the other very, very fast. They've got to be really, really intelligent.

"So the centres are being asked to do so much more than they ever used to. At the same time, you've got to get the ball back off the opposition. One thing that pleased me last week was our backline, how many times they won the ball, they were physical and I want the backline to be physical, I want them to get the ball back. The way the game is constructed right now, you don't want to be defending for lots of phases, so you've got to get the ball back. And who is involved in a lot of those phases? The centres."

Joseph is a centre by trade but has also featured regularly on the wing throughout his career.

The sibling of 54-cap international Jonathan, the younger Joseph brother featured off the bench as a youngster on the 2022 tour to Australia under Eddie Jones but is in line for his first cap under Borthwick.

Explaining Joseph's inclusion, he said: "There was a moment in training last week whenn Will got the ball and we had one of our most athletic defenders opposite in 3-4 metres of space. Will stood him up and went round him in that channel and he didn't get a hand laid on him to run away and score a try.

"Training can be loud - people are shouting the attacks, communicating the defences and people coaching - and there was this moment when that happened when there was a silence around the training field.

"I don't think I have ever heard that before. We have got the best players in England and they have just seen something happen, have been stunned by it and then celebrated it whichever team we were on."

articles.title: Rapoport: Chargers Blocked Mack Trade To Bears
articles.summary: Ian Rapoport explains why the Khalil Mack deal died. The Chargers refused to move him, and Chicago spent its picks elsewhere.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears wanted Khalil Mack back, but the deal never happened because the Los Angeles Chargers refused to sell. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confirmed on Thursday that the veteran pass rusher was never close to a trade to his old team. The Bears spent their best draft picks on Jeffery Simmons instead, leaving them with no ammo to offer Los Angeles for a reunion.

Rapoport admitted he watched the possibility of a Mack return for weeks and thought Chicago was the likely destination. "Here's one I was watching not just today, but over the last couple of weeks is Khalil Mack to the Chicago Bears," Rapoport said, according to Heavy.com . Despite the interest, the Chargers had a firm plan to keep their star player. "The Chargers never wanted to deal Khalil Mack," Rapoport explained. "They never got close to dealing Khalil Mack."

Los Angeles valued Mack as a mentor for their young pass rushers and did not want to lose that leadership. Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters he wanted Mack to remain in the locker room. Harbaugh stated, "I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He's one of the pillars of our team." The Chargers knew they could not let him go for just any draft compensation.

Chicago had already used up its draft capital before the deadline arrived. The team gave up their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth-round pick to land Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans. Rapoport noted that once the Simmons deal was done, the Bears could not make another big move. "And then for the Chicago Bears, once they did the Jeffery Simmons deal, that was kind of it," Rapoport said.

The pass rush has improved since Simmons arrived, which may have made the Mack trade less urgent anyway. Over the past two contests, the Bears have recorded 28 pressures and 7.0 sacks since Simmons joined. Ben Johnson said on ESPN 1000 that the defense is playing really well and Dennis Allen deserves credit for the game plans. Johnson added, "I think we can get pressure whether we send blitzes or whether we just send four, at this point."

Mack has recorded only three sacks in his first four games this season and has not managed any since. The Bears secured a 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, November 8, at Soldier Field.

articles.title: Cowboys Get Zero Calls On Pickens Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Dallas missed out on trade buzz for George Pickens. The silence speaks volumes about the team's roster confidence and injury reality.
articles.body:
The phone lines at AT&T Stadium stayed completely quiet when the NFL trade deadline arrived. Despite weeks of speculation, the Dallas Cowboys received zero calls about trading wide receiver George Pickens. This silence confirms the front office feels secure with their current roster, even with a 4-5 record. The lack of offers suggests other teams do not see Pickens as a high-value asset right now. The Dallas Morning News reported that the franchise received no phone calls regarding the wide receiver, according to two people with knowledge of the situation.

Coach Brian Schottenheimer has his hands full with a squad that is physically broken. Eight players sat out practice on Wednesday, leaving the team with very few healthy options. The injury list includes key names like Jake Ferguson, Joey Porter Jr., and Pickens himself. Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson both missed practice because they suffered knee injuries during the win over the Colts. Schottenheimer said on Monday that both players would miss multiple weeks of action.

The team simply cannot risk trading a player when they have so many bodies on the sidelines. Pickens was listed as limited in practice due to a hamstring issue. He also missed the game against Indianapolis last Sunday. The coaching staff is trying to manage a long list of banged-up players who need to be ready for the 49ers. Schottenheimer explained the situation clearly when he said, "Got a bunch of guys banged up. And see who moves around okay today."

Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams is one of the few bright spots who is healthy and playing at a high level. He has recorded four sacks and 10 tackles for loss over his last four games. His focus remains on stopping the San Francisco offense, not on making roster moves. Williams stated that he wants to win no matter what team they play or when the game takes place.

Yahoo Sports suggests this quiet deadline sends a specific message to the coaching staff. The team did not add any significant depth, leaving Schottenheimer with the exact roster he had before the deadline. Only running back Kendre Miller was signed to the practice squad to fill a gap left by Tyler Goodson. The franchise has to make the current group work or accept the consequences of a losing season.

The Cowboys face a massive test this Sunday against a 7-1 San Francisco 49ers team. The game is set for 3:25 p.m. CT at AT&T Stadium on Fox. Dallas needs to find a way to get healthy players on the field to have any chance. Schottenheimer noted regarding the injured Porter Jr., "The most important thing is trying to find a way to make sure we get him on the field."

articles.title: Former Super Bowl champion coach says Giants look like a ‘really urgent group’
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin says the Giants (5-2-1), who sit in first place in the NFC East heading into Thursday night’s game with the Washington Commanders, look like a “r...
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin, the former Super Bowl winning coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, has noticed one aspect of the Giants under coach John Harbaugh that he believes is being under-reported.

Tomlin says the Giants (5-2-1), who sit in first place in the NFC East heading into Thursday night's home game with the Washington Commanders, look like a "really urgent group."

"I don't know that John was ever lacking in intensity or energy, but I've certainly seen what he's infused into that collective," Tomlin said Wednesday on an NBC call with reporters. "It's displayed not only in their play, but there was an image the other week of their sideline and how everyone was engaged. There were guys running with the runner along the sideline.

"I just think that speaks to what he's done for them in terms of making them appreciate the urgency required to win and win consistently."

He added: "When I look at them, I see a really urgent group. We don't give that enough of analysis in terms of how it impacts games. Teams that play hard, teams that are urgent, teams that are willing to fight -- I just think that those are some of the things that I've seen John consistently instill in the teams that he leads, and I see it in New York."

The Giants should be urgent. After all, they haven't won the NFC East since 2011, but now they are in prime position to do so despite starting three quarterbacks this season.

Tight end Chris Manhertz told Darryl Slater of NJ.com one key to the Giants' success so far is that Harbaugh emphasizes late-game situations during practice.

"Once the game time comes, we've seen it before," Manhertz said. "It gives us a boost of confidence that no matter what happens throughout these games, we have the ability to finish.

"It gives us confidence that we can pull ourselves out of anything, if we do what we're supposed to do. When certain things happen, no matter what, we don't blink — because we know that we have the ability to finish."
