articles.title: How ASU football can take down UCF's 'attack' mentality in key road test
articles.summary: Arizona State has had a few lengthy road trips this season. They'll face another at Central Florida in Orlando.
articles.body:
The Arizona State Sun Devils have had a few lengthy road trips this season. They'll face another when they travel across the country for the first time to take on Central Florida in Orlando.

The Sun Devils have not won back-to-back games. They also haven't lost back-to-back games. But that means their record is hovering around .500. They are coming off a 20-10 win over visiting Colorado so they have a chance to put together consecutive wins for the first time.

Coach Kenny Dillingham isn't taking his opponent lightly.

"Speed stands out," he said. "Explosiveness, they're multiple on both sides of the ball offensively. They do a great job with formations and shifts and motions and shot getting guys down the field. They ran a two-by-two slot post the other night, but they released the boundary tight end to pull the quarter safety down. ...

"Sometimes you face teams and they kind of just do what they do. I think this is a very purposeful offense. They do things to attack what you're in, as opposed to like this, if we're running this regardless."

See game action from Arizona State vs Colorado football in photos

Let'a take a closer look at the matchup:

Arizona State (5-4, 3-3) at Central Florida (5-4, 3-3)

Time/site : 1:30 a.m. MST, Saturday, Nov. 14, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Fla.

TV: ESPN2, Chuckie Kempf, play by play, and Dustin Fox, analyst.

Radio : ESPN 620 AM . Tim Healey, Jeff Van Raaphorst, Kevin Turner, Jeff Munn.

Series history : ASU leads 2-0. The previous meetings were in 2024 and 2002. Both were played in Tempe.

Last meeting: ASU defeated the Knights 35-31 in 2024, the year it went on to win the Big 12.

The teams sit with the same overall and conference records, and both are one game from bowl eligibility.

Both have injuries to key players. Central Florida will be without its top running back, Duke Watson, who was injured in last week's game.

ASU will be without two of its starters in the back end of the secondary, Lyrik Rawls and Rodney Bimage, both out for the season.

The teams have three common opponents: BYU, Baylor, and Kansas. Central Florida defeated BYU (39-31 in 2 OT) and Kansas (33-32) and lost to Baylor (41-9). ASU also beat Kansas (24-17), but lost to BYU (27-20) and Baylor (55-19).

Kenny Dillingham, ASU (fourth year, 27-21) : Dillingham, 36, was the Big 12 Coach of the Year in 2024, the season when ASU won the conference championship.

Scott Frost, Central Florida (fourth year, second year back in second stint, 29-18 at UCF, 45-49 overall ): Frost, 51, was at UCF in 2016 and 2017, leading the Knights to a 13-0 mark in 2017. That led to job at Nebraska, which lasted five years and didn't go well (18-22). He returned to UCF in 2025 after one year working for the Los Angeles Rams staff.

It can hold a lead: The Knights have had trouble closing out games. Last week, the Knights led Kansas, 26-7, going into the fourth quarter and blew the lead, needing a score on the last play of the game to win it. Earlier this season they had a 17-0 lead over Houston in the third quarter, only to give up 27 unanswered points and lost that game, 27-17.

The offensive line holds up : Sun Devils faithful know what it is like to have an offensive line that is suspect. In the last two games, UCF has given up 11 sacks and 23 tackles for a loss, both alarming numbers. This could be just what the doctor ordered as ASU's defensive line has had improved defensive line play and pass rush in recent outings. Some injuries to this unit have factored in the struggles as of late.

Alonza Barnett plays well : The UCF quarterback played the first two games, then missed the next six with a significant hamstring injury. He returned last week.

Jake Fette continues his development: This will be just Fette's third start and he's a true freshman so there is a learning curve. He showed improvement last week over his first start at BYU. He needs to keep the trajectory going upward. Dillingham has been pleased with the maturity he has shown and that he has run the offense like a veteran, free of any pre-snap penalties or other errors that can come with having a rookie in the position.

It can run the ball: The Sun Devils rank 95th out of 138 FBS schools in rushing offense (136.6 ypg). That doesn't quite measure up to how ASU has fared there in the past. The turnover up front has something to do with that. True freshman Cardae Mack had 25 carries last week, and Dillingham admitted that's heavier workload than they'd like to see for one guy, let alone a newcomer. UCF ranks 59th in rushing defense (133.8 ypg).

The back end of the defense hold up : ASU is missing two starters, Rawls and Bimage, both of whom are out for the season. The Sun Devils are giving up 212.8 yards per game through the air and UCF is averaging 219.6.

Arizona State : DL My'Keil Gardner, TE Khamari Anderson, LB Zyrus Fiaseu, DB Nigel Pringle, S Lyrik Rawls, CB Rodney Bimage are all out for the season. WR Harry Hassmann is also out. RB Jason Brown, OL Wade Helton and WR Uriah Neloms are questionable.

Central Florida: DB D.J. Bell, DB Demari Henderson, DB Kahmel Johnson, RB Duke Watson, OL Tyler Gibson, TE Dylan Burk are questionable.

0 —Number of penalties the Knights had in last week's win over Kansas. It marked the second time doing so in program history and the first time since Nov. 3, 2007 in a 47-13 win over Marshall in Orlando. They have been called for 50 penalties for 385 yards on the season, an average of 42.7 yards per game. ASU has 43 for 389 yards, an average of 43.2.

9 — ASU's Reed Harris has nine touchdown catches and 907 receiving yards on 52 catches. The touchdowns are tied for fifth in ASU history through nine games, and the yards rank fifth. Harris leads the Big 12 in receiving yards and yards per game (100.8). His 103 yards against Colorado pushed him to 2,068 for his career.

13 —Tackles needed for ASU linebacker Owen Long to reach 300 for his career. His 91 this season rank him sixth among all FBS defenders.

36 — Consecutive games started for ASU defensive tackle C.J. Fite. That's the longest streak on the team. He has played in 47 and started in 41 in his three-plus years.

51 —ASU has 51 passes defended through nine games, tied for 10th nationally: 46 pass breakups and five interceptions. Ashton Stamps recorded his first career interception against Colorado. The Sun Devils' 14.1 percent forced incompletion rate is tied for third in the FBS, and their defensive backs' 7.6 percent havoc rate ranks 16th. ASU allows 4.3 yards after the catch per completion, sixth-lowest in the nation.

ASU offensive coordinator Marcus Arroyo on the work Jake Fette is putting in off the field: "The dark hours is what we call it. It's the time where a lot of people won't do what you need to do. That's just gaining extra time, extra tidbits, and he's been awesome. Getting kind of a CliffsNotes version of where you can find those minutes. He's been really good with that, and I think that says a lot about him."

Central Florida coach Scott Frost on ASU: "They've settled in on a quarterback who's young but playing pretty well. Their defense is longer and more athletic than what we saw last week. They run to the ball really well. It's going to be a challenge on both sides of the football. Just like last week, and the week before, teams in this league are pretty evenly matched and you gotta play really well every week."

Arizona State 27, Central Florida 24 : This should be a close game as evidenced by the teams having the same records. They're also close in most statistical categories. The areas in which UCF has struggled play right into ASU's strengths.

articles.title: Which Texoma high school football teams face the toughest playoff paths?
articles.summary: From Windthorst to Legacy, see which Wichita Falls-area football teams face the toughest roads through the UIL Texas high school playoffs.
articles.body:
Every player dreams of hoisting a state championship trophy.

The road to Arlington, Texas, though, is rarely straightforward, and for some Wichita Falls-area football teams, the toughest obstacles could arrive long before December.

Northside opens the postseason against undefeated Gordon, while Munday and Seymour face opponents with just one loss apiece. Meanwhile, perennial contenders Graham, Windthorst, Jacksboro and Muenster enter the playoffs with championship aspirations of their own, though their paths could become considerably more challenging as the brackets narrow.

With the UIL bi-district playoffs kicking off Thursday, here's a look at which Texoma teams face the toughest roads to a state championship and the potential matchups standing between them and a title.

Legacy and Memorial compete in crosstown showdown

Legacy's first playoff appearance in program history comes with a challenging road through Class 5A Division II.

The Leopards open against El Paso Chapin (7-3), which enters the postseason riding a six-game winning streak after capturing its district championship. Legacy, meanwhile, secured its playoff berth with a convincing 55-17 victory over Memorial in the regular-season finale.

A win would send the Leopards into an area-round matchup against the winner of Colleyville Heritage (6-4) and Frisco.

The "deep end of the pool" includes Amarillo Palo Duro (9-1), which handed Legacy a 50-9 defeat during district play, along with Lovejoy (9-1) and undefeated Anna (10-0).

For a program making its postseason debut, the challenge is considerable. Legacy must first navigate a difficult road trip to El Paso before potentially encountering some of the strongest teams in Class 5A Division II.

Few area teams face a more daunting road through their region than Windthorst.

The seventh-ranked Trojans enter the Class 2A Division II playoffs riding a seven-game winning streak, but Region II features several championship contenders who can end their season.

Windthorst opens against Quanah (4-6), setting up a potential second-round meeting with Stamford (7-3). A victory there could put the Trojans on a collision course with No. 9 Wellington (8-1) in the regional semifinals.

And even if Windthorst survives those challenges, undefeated Goldthwaite (10-0), ranked sixth in the Dave Campbell's Texas Football poll, will likely await in the regional championship. The Trojans could have to defeat two state-ranked opponents in consecutive rounds just to reach the state semifinals.

Northside doesn't have the luxury of easing into the postseason.

Despite losing just once during the regular season, the Indians open the Class 1A Division I playoffs against undefeated Gordon (9-0), the state's second-ranked team.

Gordon's unbeaten record makes the Longhorns one of the area's most difficult first-round opponents, regardless of classification. The challenge for Northside isn't necessarily how many ranked teams could appear later in the bracket. It's surviving the first 48 minutes against a program with legitimate state championship aspirations.

Munday's postseason begins with a familiar challenge: finding a way past one of the strongest teams in Class 2A Division II.

The Moguls drew Wellington (8-1), which enters the playoffs ranked ninth. Wellington's only loss came against undefeated Gruver, one of the leading state championship contenders in the classification. Should Munday pull off the upset, the winner of Crawford (7-3) and Albany (7-3) would await in the area round.

The difficulty only increases from there, with Windthorst and Stamford occupying the other side of the regional semifinal bracket.

For the Moguls, an extended postseason run could require navigating several teams with seven or more victories before even reaching the regional championship.

Seymour faces another difficult opening assignment in Class 2A Division II.

The Panthers begin their postseason against Wheeler (8-1), which enters the playoffs with one of the strongest records in Region II.

A victory would send Seymour into an area-round matchup against the winner of Santo (9-1) and Miles (5-5), potentially creating consecutive games against opponents with a combined 17 regular-season victories.

And with undefeated No. 6 Goldthwaite (10-0) looming as a potential regional semifinal opponent, Seymour's path offers little room for error.

Graham has already seen what one of the state's strongest Class 4A Division II contenders can do.

The Steers' only regular-season loss came against Brock, 59-7, in Week 10. Now, the two programs could meet again with a trip to the state semifinals on the line.

But Graham has plenty to navigate before a potential rematch.

The Steers open against Lubbock Estacado (8-2), one of the strongest first-round opponents facing any nine-win team in the area. A victory would set up an area-round matchup against the winner of El Paso Irvin (6-4) and Pecos (5-5).

Their half of Region I also features Mineral Wells (8-2), Seminole (7-3) and Levelland (7-3), while undefeated Lubbock-Cooper Liberty (10-0) and Brock (9-1) occupy the opposing half.

A potential rematch with Brock would have to come in the regional championship, giving Graham plenty of work to do before another shot at the team responsible for its only defeat.

Jacksboro might have one of the more favorable opening matchups among the area's top contenders, but the Tigers' path could become considerably more challenging.

The eighth-ranked Tigers begin the Class 3A Division II playoffs against Grape Creek (2-8), which won just twice during the regular season. A victory would set up a second-round matchup against the winner of Childress (6-4) and Littlefield (7-3), with Friona (7-3), Slaton (6-4), Stanton (6-4) and Henrietta (5-5) among the other teams in Jacksboro's half of Region I.

The biggest challenge could come in the regional championship, where undefeated No. 1 Idalou (10-0) and Canadian (7-3) are among the potential opponents.

Jacksboro has a manageable opening draw on paper, but a trip to the state semifinals will require getting past the top-ranked team in Class 3A Division II.

articles.title: Rockets Guard Ejected After Punching Warriors Player in Heated Moment During NBA Game
articles.summary: Marcus Smart was tossed from the game after he punched Charles Bassey in the waning seconds of the third quarter on Wednesday night in Houston
articles.body:
Marcus Smart was ejected from the game after punching Warriors player Charles Bassey

The Houston Rockets guard left the court before the flagrant 2 foul was handed out

Smart joined the Rockets in the offseason on a free agent deal after one season with the Lakers

Marcus Smart was ejected for throwing a punch at Golden State Warriors player Charles Bassey during a game on Wednesday night.

The Houston Rockets guard, 32, did not wait for the referees' official review before leaving for the locker room, seconds after he punched Bassey in the third quarter.

Officials ruled the contact a flagrant foul 2, which prompted an automatic ejection from the game.

Things got chippy between the two after the Rockets' Amen Thompson scored on a layup to extend Houston's lead with 21 seconds to go in the third.

As Smart and Bassey got into it, Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg was seen trying to separate them.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

According to Rockets coach Ime Udoka, Smart said Bassey was targeting his previously injured elbow.

But after the game, Bassey elaborated on what he believed initiated the fracas.

"I remember the first half, I was trying to set a screen [and] he grabbed my knee," Bassey, 26, said. "He was playing dirty. I think I was trying to get a rebound. He was grabbing my hand, and I was trying to run back on defense. Then he got up on me and just swung. Obviously, that was weak. I just think that was, honestly, fake toughness."

He added, "It didn't surprise me. I knew he was going to do something. I don't think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. I think he was trying to chill. He wasn't trying to hoop. That was fake toughness."

Smart joined the Rockets over the summer in free agency after one season on the Los Angeles Lakers.

The ejection was his 13th of his 12-year career which has included nine seasons with the Boston Celtics and stints with the Memphis Grizzlies and Washington Wizards.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum’s Brutal Honesty After Celtics Win Over Raptors
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum called his own game terrible despite leading the Celtics past the Raptors. See the stats and quotes from Wednesday night.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics refused to roll over on Wednesday night, overcame a 22-point deficit against the Toronto Raptors. Boston won 98-93, extending their winning streak to five games even with Paul George sidelined by illness. This comeback was the second biggest in the Joe Mazzulla era, per Yahoo Sports , and it proves the team has a killer instinct when things go wrong.

Jayson Tatum led the charge with 24 points, eight assists, and seven rebounds, yet he refused to accept praise for his effort. The star forward shot just 6 for 21 from the field and 2 for 11 from deep, numbers that usually signal a bad night. Instead of making excuses, Tatum offered a scathing self-evaluation that every fan needs to hear. "I played like sh*t all game, especially in the second half," Tatum said after the game, per Yahoo Sports. "So I just kind of wanted to do my part."

Toronto built a huge lead early because their bench players played with zero fear. All five Raptors reserves finished with a positive plus-minus, a rare feat that kept Boston on its heels for the first half. The starters for Toronto simply could not maintain that energy when it mattered most.

Without Scottie Barnes or Kawhi Leonard, the Raptors lacked a true table-setter to drive into the paint. Ja'Kobe Walter led the team with 17 points, but the offense went ice cold in the second half. The team managed only 32 points after halftime, a sharp drop from the 38 they scored in the first quarter. This lack of rhythm from the starters ultimately cost them the game, according to Sports Illustrated .

This victory is not just about the record; it is about how Boston handles adversity on the road. The Celtics are now 10-2, matching their start from the championship season in 2024. By playing in every single back-to-back game so far this season, Tatum has demonstrated a willingness to test his limits. "It's my 10th year, so I understand the balance of wanting to play every game, and rest, and back-to-backs," Tatum told reporters, per CelticsBlog . "We have a plan. I don't really like sitting out on away games, but we just kind of figure it out as we go."

The win extends the Celtics' dominance over Atlantic Division foes, improving their record to 4-0 against those teams. Tatum hit a huge mid-range jumper over RJ Barrett with 1:55 left to go, giving Boston a one-point lead that they would not surrender. That shot, combined with clutch free throws from Tatum in the final seconds, sealed the deal. According to the Associated Press, the Raptors dropped to 5-6, marking their first time this season falling below .500.

articles.title: 49ers pursued massive trade for star wide receiver
articles.summary: The 49ers were looking for wide receiver help at the NFL trade deadline, and before they acquired Keenan Allen, they were interested in someone else.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers were desperate for help at wide receiver at this year's NFL trade deadline after losing Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel to injuries.

While San Francisco ended up acquiring Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts for a sixth-round pick, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini , they also showed some interest in New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson.

"A trade never was a realistic possibility even though the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers were interested," Cimini said. "Wilson didn't want to leave, and the Jets didn't want to deal arguably their best player. Under contract through 2030, he's viewed as a foundational piece."

Wilson, 26, plaed at Ohio State from 2019-21, earning All-Big Ten honors twice before New York took him in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft. In 66 games over five years, he's caught 358 passes for 4,171 yards and 21 touchdowns.

Allen is near the end of his career and is on a one-year deal, so the cost to add him was a lot less than it was to add the younger Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million extension in 2025 that ties him to a team through 2030.

articles.title: Packers' Matt LaFleur blown away by the price Vikings paid for Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: LaFleur admitted he was shocked that the Raiders didn't get more for Cousins.
articles.body:
With an injury to Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz's stinker on Monday night, it became quite predictable the Vikings would hit the trade market for a QB ahead of Tuesday's deadline. They did exactly that when they brought back Kirk Cousins in a swap with the Raiders.

While the idea of the Vikings bringing in a quarterback wasn't entirely surprising, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was admittedly stunned at how little it cost the Vikings to land Cousins.

"I'm surprised they didn't get more for him, quite honestly," LaFleur said Wednesday at his press conference. "I was shocked what they traded him for. It was mind-blowing to me."

articles.title: Dupont thrust into France flyhalf role against Springboks with only one training run
articles.summary: PARIS (AP) — Captain Antoine Dupont has had one training run as France's emergency flyhalf for the showdown with world champion South Africa on Friday in rug...
articles.body:
PARIS (AP) — Captain Antoine Dupont has had one training run as France's emergency flyhalf for the showdown with world champion South Africa on Friday in rugby's Nations Championship.

Regarded as the world's best scrumhalf, Dupont was the novel stopgap choice at flyhalf after Romain Ntamack dislocated his shoulder against Fiji last Saturday, piling on to France's injured No. 10s Matthieu Jalibert, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy.

Maxime Lucu, Dupont's regular backup scrumhalf, comfortably played the last 50 minutes against Fiji at flyhalf.

But in the clash between the hemisphere leaders on Friday night, Lucu will be at scrumhalf and passing to Dupont at the Stade de France.

The captain has started at flyhalf in a handful of professional games for his Toulouse club, and shone in a couple, but never begun a test match in the 10 jersey.

"It was a choice that we (he and coach Fabien Galthié) discussed together," Dupont said on Thursday at the captain's run. "We didn't have a lot of time to think about it either: We had to make this decision quickly then test this combination on a single training session.

"These are two very different positions, but also very linked. With Maxime, we both have this versatility. So we tried to exchange and prepare ourselves as much as possible to adapt. We also worked on some things in our only available training, building on our respective knowledge of these positions. We looked for the combination that could work best for the team, with maximum adaptation.

"Everyone has different qualities and we're working to allow the team to play its best. It will be, above all, a question of adaptation."

South Africa counterpart Siya Kolisi wasn't surprised by Dupont's shift.

"He's played there before for his club, and he played very well. He can play almost anywhere on the field and he's a good enough player to do it," Kolisi said.

But neither was Kolisi fazed by what Dupont and Lucu can or will do. The Springboks expect the pair to swap places during the match to speed up their attack.

"Our system doesn't change for any team we play against," Kolisi said.

"We've watched clips and seen how they play, and we've watched how he plays at flyhalf, too, so we haven't done anything special for him individually because he's playing at No 10.

"Maxime Lucu has also played flyhalf for Bordeaux, so it will happen naturally for them to swap. Antoine wants to be on the ball a lot and he creates a lot of play on the field, so for him to go to scrumhalf will also be natural, and they'll be able to adjust. That said, our system is prepared for that."

The Springboks have won nine of the last 10 matches with France. They haven't lost to France in Paris in 21 years. Dupont has tasted victory against South Africa only once.

He noted that beating the Boks will have to start, as always, up front.

"They are a team that loses very little and is particularly difficult to beat. But they can be caught out like every team," Dupont said. "They very often manage to make up for their mistakes thanks to their collective strength. We will try to find flaws in their game, there are solutions to them.

"Once again, we will first have to take up the physical challenge and win our collisions. Then, we will have to be constantly reading the game and able to seize opportunities. They will probably be few in number but we will have to be as pragmatic as possible when we have them."

articles.title: Readers Slam TPC Scottsdale And St Andrews As Overrated
articles.summary: GolferInsight readers name the 10 most overrated courses, with TPC Scottsdale and St Andrews leading the list of disappointing layouts.
articles.body:
Golfers often pay a premium for the promise of a perfect round, only to leave with a sinking feeling. MyGolfSpy released a fresh report listing the 10 most overrated golf courses based on their forum community, underscoring this annoyance. The list includes legendary names that usually draw praise, yet readers claim these specific layouts fail to match their hype. The data comes from a direct poll of the MyGolfSpy forum, where members shared their most memorable letdowns.

TPC Scottsdale topped the list as the most overrated course. Forum members described the layout as feeling pedestrian when the tournament atmosphere is absent. The Blue Monster at Doral ranked second, with readers citing a price that does not match the experience. Even St Andrews made the cut, surprising many given its global status. The report notes that every course on the list has defenders, proving that enjoyment remains deeply subjective. Still, the consensus suggests golfers should know exactly what they are getting into before booking a tee time at these venues.

The core issue identified by the community is the gap between reputation and reality. MyGolfSpy explained that while top courses usually deliver, some leave players feeling let down despite high expectations. To compile this final ranking, the forum members evaluated how often courses were nominated alongside the particular reasons provided. While some of the biggest names in golf garnered multiple nominations, other courses were highlighted for distinct, unforgettable bad experiences. This approach ensures the list reflects a broad range of opinions rather than just a few outliers.

Readers pointed out that conditioning, architecture, and scenery sometimes fail to justify the cost. The MyGolfSpy team previously wrote about seven overrated courses, but this new list focuses entirely on community feedback. The beauty of the story lies in the fact that a course topping this list could be someone's absolute favorite. However, the goal is to provide transparency for the average golfer planning a trip. When the hype is high, the risk of a disappointing round increases significantly.

The data comes from the first installment of a new series by MyGolfSpy, which reached out to their Forum community for responses. The final list contains exactly 10 courses that generated the most interesting criticism. TPC Scottsdale led the pack, followed closely by the Blue Monster at Doral. The report explicitly mentions St Andrews as a course that made the list despite its history. This inclusion signals that even the most hallowed grounds are not immune to criticism from those who play them regularly.

MyGolfSpy emphasized that the list was not about destroying reputations but about calling out places that do not meet expectations. The community shared experiences where the price paid did not align with the quality received. This feedback loop allows the site to keep content mostly positive while occasionally addressing the darker side of golf travel. The 10 courses named represent a mix of public and private tracks, showing that no type of ownership is safe from these complaints.

Golf course enjoyment is deeply subjective, a point MyGolfSpy stressed throughout the report. A layout that frustrates one player might delight another. The report acknowledges that all 10 courses on the list have defenders who would argue they are world-class. This subjectivity makes the list more about managing expectations than declaring a final verdict on quality. Golfers should view the list as a guide to potential pitfalls rather than a definitive ranking of bad courses.

The analysis suggests that the "sinking feeling" of a letdown often stems from the gap between expectation and reality. When players pay a premium for a highly touted layout, the pressure to perform is higher. If the course lacks the tournament atmosphere or fails to deliver on conditioning, the disappointment is magnified. MyGolfSpy noted that the forum community provided the most interesting criticism, helping to curate a list that resonates with real-world experiences.

For the average golfer, knowing which courses generate the most criticism can help in planning a trip. The report is a warning to research the current state of a course before booking. While St Andrews and TPC Scottsdale remain iconic, the community feedback highlights specific reasons why they might not live up to the hype for every visitor.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor addresses Colts trade deadline decision to keep him
articles.summary: On Thursday, RB Jonathan Taylor discussed the Colts' trade deadline decision to keep him.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline has passed, and Jonathan Taylor remains a member of the Indianapolis Colts despite heavy trade speculation.

Over the previous week, even Taylor was uncertain of what the future would hold. But now, still with the Colts , he's focused on Miami.

"Just regular schedule programming," said Taylor, via Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan. "It's all water under the bridge now."

Taylor was then asked if he was willing to be a part of the upcoming rebuild.

"Moves have already been made, it's time to go win against Miami, baby," he said.

Taylor has remained productive this season, rushing for 656 yards -- the eighth-most in the NFL -- but big plays have been tougher to come by this year. He's averaging a modest 4.1 yards per rush attempt and ranks 23rd in PFF's breakaway rate metric.

In part, that is a product of the Colts' struggling passing game. Without a vertical threat, defenses can shrink the field and play closer to the line of scrimmage. The pass game woes also put more focus on Taylor.

Moving forward, with the wide receiver room now depleted following the trade deadline moves, it's not going to get any easier for Taylor and the run game.

articles.title: ESPN Insider Urges Tigers Rival to Sign Casey Mize
articles.summary: ESPN's Jeff Passan is pushing a Tigers division rival to sign Casey Mize this winter. #Tigers
articles.body:
One of the Detroit Tigers division rivals has been pointed at a free agent Detroit knows better than anyone. In his look at the perfect 2026-27 free agency move for the teams worth watching, Jeff Passan of ESPN handed the Cleveland Guardians a name: right-handed starter Casey Mize .

Detroit traded Mize to the San Diego Padres at the Aug. 3 deadline, and the former No. 1 overall pick hit free agency when the 2026 season ended. Whether the Tigers try to bring him back is still an open question. If they do not, the team being told to go get him plays in their division.

Jeff Passan Names Casey Mize as Cleveland's Ideal Target

Passan went through the dozen returning playoff teams and five others he expects to be active, in a transaction window squeezed by the Dec. 1 lockout deadline hanging over the whole market. Cleveland went 85-77, won the AL Central and lost in the ALCS, and his pick for them was not a bat.

"While the Guardians' aggressiveness at the trade deadline helped them reach the ALCS, nobody expects them to replicate that in free agency. With the emergence of Chase DeLauter and trade for Jo Adell , their outfield is set for the first time in years. Their infield is solid, too, with the exception of first base, and between that and designated hitter, Cleveland should be in on midtier power bats.

"What the Guardians really could use is one more solid starting pitcher, preferably on a shorter-term deal, with real upside. And the ideal candidate is right there for them. Sign right-handed starter Casey Mize . "

The Guardians lost that ALCS to the Tampa Bay Rays in six games , two wins short of the pennant. Another dependable starter would not hurt a team that got that close.

Casey Mize Struggled After Leaving the Tigers

The way Mize pitched after the trade is the reason this is not a bidding war. In 10 starts with the Padres, he went 2-4 with a 7.46 ERA. He gave up 56 hits and 42 runs in 44.2 innings, walked 19, struck out 25 and carried a 1.68 WHIP.

In 16 starts for Detroit before the deadline, he was 4-6 with a 2.70 ERA. He allowed 67 hits and 27 runs in 86.2 innings, walked 19, struck out 85 and carried a 0.99 WHIP. That gap between the two halves of his season is why Passan framed the fit as a shorter-term deal with upside rather than a long commitment.

What Casey Mize's Free Agency Means for Detroit

Detroit is already watching one pitcher it drafted and developed go to market. Tarik Skubal , traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the same deadline, is a free agent, and ESPN rates him the No. 1 free agent of this offseason. Losing Mize to Cleveland on top of that would put two arms Detroit raised on other rosters, one of them inside the AL Central.

Pitching in Cleveland would keep Mize close to Detroit, and a reunion with the Tigers is still on the table. He was comfortable there in 2026, and the numbers back that up. If he pitches the way he did for Detroit instead of the way he did for San Diego, whoever signs him gets a bargain. That is the part of Passan's suggestion that should bother Tigers fans.

articles.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
articles.summary: A look at 10 aspects of Oregon's loss at Illinois and the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer.
articles.body:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday .

The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives.

As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer .

What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol.

Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday's game and the firing of Mehringer:

1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess

Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback's delight, but doing so under Oregon's current circumstances is somewhat obtuse.

Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois.

Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome.

Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference.

He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond.

Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change.

3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff

Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it's time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff.

Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach.

Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern's offensive coordinator. No, don't expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon.

But someone like him could fit perfectly.

After Saturday's game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott.

Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can't fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes.

That's less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it's easier to develop a connection with a team's more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance.

At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group.

Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely.

Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum.

Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks' 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47.

Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box.

Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss.

After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment.

"Yeah, it's a great question," he said. "It certainly wasn't successful. There's a pause in operation there, right?"

Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen?

For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches' headsets.

If Lanning didn't like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not.

The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot.

That's what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed.

Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called.

Oregon gained 180 yards on the ground against a team that ranked 12th in the Big Ten in rushing defense, allowing 134.4 yards per game.

Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn't consistently deliver.

As a result, Oregon converted on just four of 15 third-down attempts.

With most of the team's top receivers out, the rushing attack needed to be special, and it wasn't.

The junior entered the game 9-for-9 on field-goal attempts and went 1-for-4. But two of his three misses came from beyond 50 yards.

Hurych missed his first attempt from 52 yards out. He made a 20-yard field goal in the second quarter to put Oregon up 10-0. He missed a 53-yarder with 6:04 to go in the fourth quarter and later missed a 47-yarder with 52 seconds to go.

"He's human," Lanning said. "The reality is, those are long kicks. Some of those are really tough. The wind's a little bit different in this stadium. I think we put them in a position that wasn't the easiest to operate, and we've been really fortunate this year."

8. Rushing defense faltered when it mattered most.

Oregon's defense kept the Ducks in the games against UCLA and Nebraska until the offense started to come alive.

Oregon lost to the Bruins 17-15 and beat Nebraska 17-14.

On Saturday, the Ducks led 10-0 late in the second quarter. At that point, nobody knew Oregon wouldn't score again. But the defense's job was to keep dominating, just in case.

Illinois running back Aidan Laughery got loose for a 75-yard touchdown run, making it 10-7 with 2:15 left in the half. Illinois had rushed for just 14 yards before that run, but finished the game with 225 rushing yards.

That production took pressure off freshman starting quarterback Michael Clayton II, who threw for two second-half touchdowns.

A dominant defense doesn't let that happen against a team it has on the ropes.

The loss was more about the Ducks' offense than the defense. But the defense got sloppy—several defenders made mistakes on Laughery's long run—revealing a lack of four-quarter focus.

"In moments today, they played really well as well," Lanning said of his defense. "But ultimately, they still had 225 yards rushing, or whatever. The final total was there. We can play better than that."

9. Should quarterback Akili Smith Jr. get a shot?

Many fans frustrated with the quarterback play have called for Smith to get a shot. The sophomore former four-star recruit flashed some skills against Portland State and again last spring.

Is he ready to take on a Big Ten team? Only the coaches know for sure. They see him in practice every day.

Even if the Ducks have no shot at the playoffs, Lanning will likely play to win, not to develop. That means he has to believe Smith can win before Smith gets on the field.

However, if Moore does not return, Lanning should at least give Smith some game reps. Lanning said he had a Smith package ready for Nebraska, so we know Lanning has some plays he believes Smith can run effectively.

Truth be told, what do they have to lose? Raiola has been so inconsistent that giving Smith a series or two couldn't hurt much.

10. The team appeared to be deflated after the game.

Understandably, Oregon left Illinois dejected. It will be interesting to see how the team responds. The loss probably ended the Ducks' playoff chances.

Although a 9-3 team could qualify for the playoffs given the level of national parity, Oregon winning nine games appears unlikely.

With many players returning this season to make a national title run and key players with NFL futures to consider, it's conceivable that many players shut down emotionally for the season.

It's doubtful that many marquee players have any interest in playing in a random bowl game. Those headed to the NFL or the transfer portal wouldn't play in a bowl game anyway.

If the team loses its zeal, the Ducks could fail to win seven games in a full season for the first time since 2016, when Oregon went 4-8.

articles.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
articles.summary: Illinois lost its starting quarterback and will turn to a true freshman against the Ducks.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation.

Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10.

Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks' 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26.

However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks.

A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team's bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton.

"It was just good timing," Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session.

Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation's best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions.

Now Illinois heads into Saturday's game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed.

His performance against MSU elevated expectations.

Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31.

Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass.

Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter.

Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd's inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week.

"I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep," Bielema said.

Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job.

"I've said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program," Bielema said.

Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances.

"He knows he's going to play now," Lunney told reporters.

"We feel like we have another guy on campus in that room that can help us win and we're very confident in that," Bielema said.

Oregon coach Dan Lanning said it's difficult to scout Clayton given his limited body of work. Oregon has watched some of his high school game film. But mostly, Oregon will focus on Illinois' system.

"There might be wrinkles, but very rarely do people change the identity of their offense based on a change of the position," Lanning said. "So you prepare and then you make sure you have answers for what you think that skill set is."

If Moore doesn't return this week, Raiola and Thomas will compete for the starting job against Illinois.

Raiola replaced Moore at USC and thrived in the win, but following a bye, struggled for three quarters during a 17-15 loss to UCLA on Oct. 10. Thomas performed better in the fourth quarter and almost pulled out the victory.

Thomas started Saturday's 17-14 home win over Nebraska, but struggled for three quarters before Lanning turned to Raiola. He led the Ducks from a 14-6 deficit to a win with a four-yard touchdown pass to tight end Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds remaining.

Lanning said he's confident in all four quarterbacks, including sophomore Akili Smith Jr., who had a play package ready for Nebraska if needed.

Illinois is most familiar with Raiola, who, as a Nebraska freshman in 2024, passed for 297 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in a 31-24 overtime loss to Illinois.

"Raiola is obviously a very accomplished player," Bielema said. "Kind of almost unusual. You got to almost prepare for possibly three quarterbacks on Saturday. But we'll kind of handle that during the course of the week and see where that goes."

Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) at Illinois (3-3, 1-2)

Where: Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign, Ill.

articles.title: Dan Hicks Celebrated Daughter’s Marathon Finish in Final Instagram Post Before His ‘Unexpected’ Death
articles.summary: Hicks shared three daughters with his wife, Hannah Storm
articles.body:
Dan Hicks celebrated his daughter's finish in the Chicago Marathon in his final post on Instagram

"Our girl did it again," Hicks wrote on Oct. 11 after his daughter's race

Hicks' wife Hannah Storm announced his death in a post on Thursday, Nov. 12

One month before his unexpected death at 64, Dan Hicks proudly celebrated his daughter Riley's finish in the Chicago Marathon.

The longtime NBC Sports announcer's final post on Instagram was a three-image carousel shared on Sunday, Oct. 11, captioned, "Our girl did it again. 3rd major marathon in 18 months. Today she tackled Chicago and we were there to marvel at her drive in hot weather and smashing her PR!"

Hicks posted a video of Riley running in the marathon in the first slide and a photo of her smiling while posing with her medal and a bouquet of flowers in the second.

The third slide showed a sweet photo after the race of Hicks posing with Riley and his other daughter, Ellery, who he shares with his wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm . The couple are also parents to Hannah Hicks.

Storm, 64, shared the news in a statement on social media on Thursday, Nov. 12. She said her husband's death was "sudden and unexpected."

"Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness," Storm continued. "He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable."

She described Dan as "truly one of a kind, and quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around."

"When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered," said Storm, who announced on Oct. 28 that she was officially "cancer-free" after undergoing a recent hysterectomy .

Hicks had worked for NBC as a sports broadcaster since 1992, joining the network after starting his career at KVOA in Tuscon, Ariz., and later CNN.

Tributes began pouring in shortly after Hicks' family confirmed his death. Olympic skier Lindsey Vonn said, "This is hard to believe. Dan was the best. RIP my friend. You will be missed," in an Instagram Story.

articles.title: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
articles.summary: Jordan Ayew has a first-half penalty saved as Ghana secure a comfortable 2-0 home win over Somalia to kick-start their Afcon 2027 qualifying campaign.
articles.body:
Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia.

The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent.

Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals.

The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein.

Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out.

Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line.

The result puts the four-time continental champions three points behind Ivory Coast and The Gambia, who meet in Bouake at 19:00 GMT.

Cameroon and Senegal are also in action later on Thursday.

Elsewhere, Newcastle United striker Yoane Wissa opened the scoring as DR Congo continued their perfect start with a 3-1 win over Sierra Leone in Kinshasa.

The Leopards are on nine points at the top of Group E, five points ahead of Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea after those two sides drew 0-0.

Nigeria were handed a boost after Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau could only manage a 1-1 draw in their away tie against Madagascar in neutral Morocco.

The Super Eagles trail Guinea-Bissau by four points ahead of their home game against Tanzania on Friday (16:00 GMT).

Tanzania are assured of a place at Afcon 2027 as tournament co-hosts, with the other three sides battling for one qualification spot.
